selection: The original curated 100 languages, expanded to cover official languages and written forms of countries and territories where complete reviewed translations are feasible.

languages.name: Akan
languages.reviewNotes: Narrowed to Asante technical loanword spelling and complex access, timeout and protocol clauses; ordinary website and polite-instruction vocabulary has published support.

languages.name: Azerbaijani (Cyrillic)
languages.reviewNotes: Same-language rendering of reviewed az. Uses modern Cyrillic orthography with Azerbaijani-specific letters; does not claim verified Dagestan administrative standard or restore every historical apostrophe.

languages.name: Bislama
languages.reviewNotes: Uses Bislama grammar and spelling distinct from Tok Pisin. Review technical loans and naturalness of longer clauses.

languages.name: Bosnian
languages.reviewNotes: Direct translation; ijekavian Bosnian terminology.

languages.name: Bosnian (Cyrillic)
languages.reviewNotes: Same-language Cyrillic rendering of the independently translated Bosnian text; tags, identifiers and placeholders retained.

languages.name: Central Kurdish (Sorani)
languages.reviewNotes: Direct Sorani clauses, not Kurmanji respelled. Review Arabic-script shaping, idiom, and technical vocabulary.

languages.name: Montenegrin
languages.reviewNotes: Ijekavian Montenegrin with accepted ś spelling; shared South Slavic forms retained where correct. Cyrillic remains a separate uncovered written form.

languages.name: Montenegrin (Cyrillic)
languages.reviewNotes: Same-language Cyrillic version of the independently translated and reviewed Montenegrin Latin profile. Montenegrin ś becomes с́ (Cyrillic с plus combining acute); standard digraphs become љ, њ and џ. Identifiers and markup preserved.
Direct Seychellois Creole wording, with common computing loans. Distinct from Haitian and Mauritian Creoles; not copied from either.
languages.name: Seselwa Creole French
languages.writtenForm: Standard written Seychellois Creole; Latin script

languages.name: Welsh
languages.reviewNotes: Welsh mutations and formal user instructions reviewed.

languages.name: Estonian
languages.reviewNotes: Source semantics and inflected technical nouns reviewed.

languages.name: Basque
languages.reviewNotes: Basque syntax and case suffixes reviewed; technical register warrants another reading.

languages.name: Persian (Dari, Afghanistan)
languages.reviewNotes: Afghan vocabulary and register; regional Persian profile. A prs alias can point here; routing does not require a duplicate translation.

languages.name: Fulah
languages.reviewNotes: Technical vocabulary is corroborated; remaining review is noun-class agreement and natural clause construction in automatic redirect, validation and abnormal-connection explanations.

languages.name: Fijian
languages.reviewNotes: Uses explanatory phrases for origin server and time limit. Review technical loanword spelling and naturalness of longer clauses.

languages.name: Faroese
languages.reviewNotes: Distinct Faroese, not Danish or Icelandic substitution. Technical register and noun-case agreement have greater uncertainty.

languages.name: West Frisian
languages.reviewNotes: West Frisian rather than Dutch or North Frisian; technical compounds and idiomatic register merit additional review.

languages.name: Irish
languages.reviewNotes: Irish vocabulary and mutations reviewed; no claim of native-language certification.

languages.name: Scottish Gaelic
languages.reviewNotes: Distinct Scottish Gaelic, not Irish substitution; technical compounds and idiomatic clauses carry additional uncertainty.

languages.name: Galician
languages.reviewNotes: Galician forms and source distinctions maintained.

Agglutinative sentence structure and new computing vocabulary remain review-sensitive. Corrected a mistaken tomorrow adverb to sapy’aitépe (shortly), redirect object, and reload phrasing. Do not treat as automatic coverage for Bolivia’s officially named Guarani; Bolivian varieties need review.
languages.name: Guarani

languages.reviewNotes: Technical circumlocutions and grammatical naturalness need further review. Native Hawaiian content was consulted for vocabulary; no claim of native fluency.
languages.name: Hawaiian
languages.writtenForm: Modern written Hawaiian; Latin script with ʻokina and kahakō

languages.name: Hmong
languages.writtenForm: White Hmong in the Romanized Popular Alphabet

languages.name: Chhattisgarhi
languages.reviewNotes: Review naturalness of the longer server-overload, request-processing and redirect sentences. Core negation and polite imperative patterns are now attested; remaining uncertainty is technical idiom, not whether this is Chhattisgarhi.

languages.name: Croatian
languages.reviewNotes: Croatian browser, server and configuration terminology; direct English-source review.

languages.name: Icelandic
languages.reviewNotes: Defensible complete text; inflection and technical register merit another linguistic reading.

languages.name: Georgian
languages.reviewNotes: Complete direct Georgian text; technical origin-server term and idiom warrant another reading.

languages.name: Kurdish (Sorani routing)
languages.reviewNotes: Direct Sorani clauses, not Kurmanji respelled. Review Arabic-script shaping, idiom, and technical vocabulary.

languages.name: Kyrgyz
languages.reviewNotes: Distinct Kyrgyz grammar and characters retained; technical-register fluency has greater uncertainty.

languages.name: Latin
languages.writtenForm: Modern Latin for technical interface text
languages.reviewNotes: Reviewed as Modern Latin technical-interface text; its transparent technical vocabulary does not claim a single Vatican-standard glossary.

languages.name: Luxembourgish
languages.reviewNotes: Luxembourgish syntax and vocabulary, with conventional technical loans; orthographic fluency should receive another reading.

languages.name: Luganda
languages.reviewNotes: Protocol-enablement wording, descriptive origin-server/load expressions, and agreement in the longer connectivity clauses still lack sufficient independent sentence-level support; basic permission, page and retry terminology is corroborated.

languages.name: Lingala
languages.reviewNotes: Review network-specific choices for origin server, configuration, domain, request and connection count, plus long error-sentence idiom. Browser/JavaScript loan usage and permission constructions are now attested.

languages.name: Latvian
languages.reviewNotes: Source semantics and case endings reviewed.

languages.name: Madurese
languages.reviewNotes: Remaining review concerns polite-register consistency, passive morphology and technical compounds; error/request/timeout/busy-server vocabulary is now externally corroborated.

languages.name: Māori
languages.writtenForm: Standard written New Zealand Māori with macrons
languages.reviewNotes: Uses established pūtirotiro/tūmau/paetukutuku vocabulary and explanatory technical clauses. Self-review clarified the number of connections; fluent idiom review remains useful.

languages.name: Macedonian
languages.reviewNotes: Direct Macedonian translation with source-semantic review.

languages.name: Mongolian
languages.writtenForm: Standard Mongolian in the Cyrillic script

languages.name: Maltese
languages.reviewNotes: Maltese morphology and conventional browser/server loanwords reviewed.
Direct Zimbabwean Ndebele draft. Similarities to Zulu follow language relationships, not copied text. Not suitable as a replacement for Southern Ndebele (nr).
languages.name: North Ndebele
languages.writtenForm: Zimbabwean isiNdebele / Northern Ndebele; Latin script

languages.name: Norwegian Nynorsk
languages.reviewNotes: Nynorsk orthography and morphology maintained; separate written form from existing Bokmål.

languages.name: Chichewa
languages.reviewNotes: Remaining concern is idiomatic browser/server/domain loanwords and configuration, timeout and connection-count clauses; basic error, submission and JavaScript instructions have published support.

languages.name: Oromo
languages.reviewNotes: Core browser/server/request and timeout terminology is corroborated; protocol-enablement wording and the longer origin-server/load clauses still need independent grammatical review.

Uses phonemic Curaçao/Bonaire spellings (ku, sirbidó, konfigurashon). Does not provide the distinct Aruban Papiamento spelling standard; pap-aw needs separate translation. pap-cw may route to this file. Technical vocabulary reviewed against published Papiamentu MediaWiki strings.
languages.name: Papiamento
Dari (Windows routing)
languages.reviewNotes: Afghan vocabulary and register; regional Persian profile. A prs alias can point here; routing does not require a duplicate translation.

languages.name: Quechua
languages.reviewNotes: Browser/server and basic permission/retry terminology is corroborated; morphology in the long origin-server, unexpected-load and protocol-enable clauses still lacks adequate independent comparison in the selected Southern Quechua written form.

languages.name: Rajasthani
languages.reviewNotes: Review agreement and idiom in borrowed technical-noun phrases, especially website suspension, redirect passives and excessive-request clauses. Core Marwari negation, possessives and case markers are now attested.

languages.name: Kirundi
languages.reviewNotes: Narrowed to browser/server/domain terminology and complex network, timeout and configuration clauses; request, regret and permission vocabulary is corroborated.

languages.name: Sanskrit
languages.reviewNotes: Technical terms include explicit server/browser loans; gender-inclusive forms are verbose. Self-review repaired agreement in configuration title. Specialist modern-technical Sanskrit review is useful.

languages.name: Scots
languages.writtenForm: Modern written Scots, broadly Central Scots
languages.reviewNotes: Conservative contemporary Scots with shared English vocabulary where correct; not Scottish English alone. No single universally fixed Scots technical orthography; technical loans retained.
languages.unchangedEnglishRationale: The phrase “Possible causes include:” consists of words and syntax shared with Scots; forced respelling would not improve fidelity.

languages.name: Slovenian
languages.reviewNotes: Source distinctions and URL clause reviewed.

languages.name: Samoan
languages.reviewNotes: Uses English server/domain/protocol loans where a speculative coinage would obscure meaning. Review technical register, glottal-stop/macron conventions and longer clauses.

languages.name: Shona
languages.reviewNotes: Remaining review is the spelling/register of bhurawuza, sevha and domeini and the original server-load, protocol and connection-count clauses; permission and ordinary browser/opening instructions are corroborated.

languages.name: Serbian (Latin)
languages.reviewNotes: Authorized same-language transliteration of existing sr, after English-source semantic review; sr.json unchanged.
Direct draft; Eswatini/South African technical idiom and agreement merit review. Removed a duplicated owner construction in both suspension descriptions.
languages.name: Swati

languages.reviewNotes: Direct draft; technical phrasing and some noun-class constructions merit review. Site unavailable retains the inability-to-use meaning; timeout explicitly refers to an elapsed wait limit.
languages.name: Southern Sotho
languages.writtenForm: Standard Sesotho / Southern Sotho; Latin script

languages.name: Tetum
languages.reviewNotes: Portuguese-derived technical vocabulary within Tetum syntax. Review accent conventions, origin-server wording and subordinate clauses.

languages.name: Tigrinya
languages.reviewNotes: Formal plural address and basic error/website terminology are corroborated. Technical configuration, protocol-enablement and long origin-server/load phrasing remain insufficiently supported.
Direct draft; changed the unavailable title from a visibility expression to inability to use. Technical register and lengthy constructions merit review.
languages.name: Tswana
Tongan
languages.writtenForm: Standard written Tongan with fakauʻa and macrons
languages.reviewNotes: Uses explanatory browser/origin-server phrases plus domain/protocol loans. Review technical register and noun/possessive phrasing.

languages.name: Tok Pisin
languages.reviewNotes: Uses descriptive origin-server wording and established English-derived technical loans. Further review should focus on request/connection wording and best-versus-better idiom.
Direct draft; noun-class agreement and technical terminology remain review-sensitive. This is not a Zulu substitution.
languages.name: Tsonga
Tatar
languages.reviewNotes: Distinct Tatar vocabulary and Cyrillic letters; not Bashkir or another Turkic substitute. Idiom and technical-register choices merit additional review.

languages.name: Uzbek (Cyrillic)
languages.reviewNotes: Same-language rendering of reviewed uz. Context-sensitive Cyrillic е/э and ё/ю/я, plus ў/ғ/ъ, reviewed word by word. Official administrative-script status remains a separate open question.

languages.name: Waray
languages.reviewNotes: Self-review repaired an incorrect apology verb and a domain/IP preposition. Review longer technical clauses and choice of borrowed terminology.

languages.name: Wolof
languages.reviewNotes: Long setup, protocol-enablement and origin-server/load clauses, including their noun-class agreement, still require stronger sentence-level support. Basic browser/server, permissions and retry terms are corroborated.

languages.name: Yoruba
languages.reviewNotes: Narrowed to modern tone marks and browser/server/protocol idiom; permission, timeout and respectful-address constructions are corroborated, and the readiness expression was corrected.

languages.name: Cantonese

languages.reviewNotes: Distinct written Cantonese in Traditional characters; serves explicit Cantonese preferences. Regional orthographic and technical-register choices remain reviewable. The legal label Chinese does not require this separate written form.

substitutionReason: Subagents could not reliably compose and review complete technical messages in the original languages without invented wording or leakage from related languages. The user chose 100 complete languages over preserving gaps in the original roster.
